surprises.head: Montréal couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Montréal usually gets some of the league’s most dangerous shots, and Washington usually gives up some of the league’s most dangerous shots. Not tonight: Montréal’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 5.0% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.7% (about 7.0% against Washington) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 25 games.

story.head: Tuch has two goals and an assist as the Capitals get past the Canadiens
paras: It was a busy first period. Josh Anderson struck first for the Canadiens early in the period, but Jordan Kyrou tied it up for Washington three and a half minutes later. Lane Hutson restored the Habs’ lead a little over three minutes later. Ivan Miroshnichenko tied it 2-2 for Washington on the power play with 26 seconds left in the first, in his first game of the season. Alex Tuch put the Capitals up 3-2 shorthanded early in the second, but Anderson scored again midway through the period to tie it 3-3. Justin Holl and Tuch scored less than five minutes apart with less than eight minutes left to put the Capitals up 5-3. With the goalie pulled and less than two minutes left, Nick Suzuki cut Washington’s lead to 5-4 on the power play, but the Capitals held on. Tuch added an assist for a three-point night.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Charlie Lindgren made 26 saves for the Capitals, and Jakub Dobeš allowed five goals on 23 shots. The Capitals improved to 4-3-0 and climbed to third in the Metropolitan, while the Canadiens fell to 3-3-1, slipping to seventh in the Atlantic.

items.text: Cole Hutson got the better of his brother Lane.
The Capitals bounced back after two straight losses.
